messages:
sam: starting a staged rollout of CUDA 12.1 images to the gpu-worker fleet in us-west-2 at 09:03. can we watch for ld-linux / symbol errors?
maria: noted. targeting the autoscale pools first (p3/p4). i've bumped node-ttl to 12h to avoid churn.
igor: seeing a few CI runs fail on reconstructed containers — crashloop with: `error while loading shared libraries: libcuda.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory`
sam: that sounds like driver mismatch. which driver version are those nodes on?
jen: quick check: driver on the node image is 525.85; CUDA 12.1 runtime in the container expects >=535 for some ABI parts. not every symbol is present.
alex: also hitting NCCL connect timeouts after warm-up at scale — looks like some nodes drop out of ring. logs: ```NCCL WARN NET/Socket : connect error (errno=111)```
maria: us-west-2 noisy neighbors + kernel patch 5.15.0-1068 triggered after the node reboot during image switch. kernel+driver/ABI mismatch might explain both libcuda missing + NCCL flakiness.
sam: action plan: 1) pause rollout, 2) cordon affected nodes, 3) spin up a canary pool with driver 535+ and CUDA12 images preloaded, 4) add fallback routing to CUDA11 variants.
jen: pausing rollout now (deploy-bot: rollout paused by jen).
deploy-bot: Rollout paused (id: r-202311-71) :thumbsup:
igor: for immediate app-level mitigation, i pushed a config to pin model-serving clusters to the cuda11-compatible image tag `redwood/runtime:1.18-cuda11` — that should reduce customer-facing errors.
alex: FYI, the container rebuilds we ran last week removed a small shim we used to set LD_LIBRARY_PATH during entrypoint — that exposes reliance on host-driver paths. we need to either restore the shim or make images self-contained.
maria: agree. long-term: images must include a minimal libcuda shim that gracefully fails with clear error and hint to driver version. short-term: restore shim patch to the Canary images.
sam: rolling back nodes with 525 drivers is not trivial (we can't downgrade kernel easily). prefer to upgrade host drivers to 535 on repro nodes. infra, can you schedule driver upgrade on a small subset?
jen: i'll schedule a driver upgrade on 3 canaries in us-west-2 now, keep them isolated from autoscaler.
igor: once canaries are green, we should run a multi-node NCCL stress for 1 hour before continuing. i have a script: ```./test_nccl_ring --gpus 8 --iters 500```
alex: cost note — running long stress tests on dedicated canaries will bump short-term spend in us-west-2. i've added a quick estimate: +$350/day for the test pool.
sam: acceptable for safety. also open a ticket to update our image build to include a driver-compat matrix in image metadata (so console can warn if host/driver < required).
maria: logged RH-3245 (infra) and assigned to eng-infra. linking to this thread.
jen: can we also add a telemetry alert for ld.so unresolved symbols in the first 30s of container start? would have caught this earlier.
igor: yes — i can add an eBPF probe that emits a metric when dlopen fails in entrypoint for `libcuda`. low noise.
sam: timeline: pause rollout (done), driver upgrade on canaries (in progress), restore shim to canary images (in progress), run NCCL stress (once canaries pass), then continue staged rollout with smaller batch size and 30m observation between batches.
alex: note for ops: region constraint — eu-west-1 uses older kernel fleet; we should hold upgrades there until we confirm host-driver compatibility matrix.
maria: putting eu-west-1 on the hold list.
jen: rollback flag prepped in deploy tooling if we detect >1% service error rate during next batch.
igor: saving logs and stack traces to /var/log/redwood/oncall/cuda12-rollout/1719123456.tar.gz.
sam: thanks all. mark this thread resolved when the canaries are green and NCCL test passes. :white_check_mark:
